svg.title: Making time for a shared activity

text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/06/20 - Essay - 01
A family spends time together.
Pexels · 5276077
Making time for a shared activity
There is more than one way to spend time with someone who cares for us. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to
others are two useful starting points.
One reason is that a simple shared activity creates space for conversation. For instance, we choose a short walk that suits
everyone’s pace. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also leaves us more time to notice what is
happening.
Another reason is that attention matters more than an elaborate plan. For example, we put our phones away and ask about a familiar
memory. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different people may need different
things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Compare two ways to spend time with someone who cares for us: a rigid plan and one that allows adjustment. Assess one advantage
and one limitation. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline:
introduce the situation; discuss a simple shared activity creates space for conversation with an example; discuss attention matters
more than an elaborate plan with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
